execution_policy.implementation_language: Rust 2024 for core; Python/Node only for optional adapters
execution_policy.rule: Complete a required milestone only when every task with required_for_core=true has completion evidence and its core milestone gates pass. Optional tasks/tracks never gate core release unless a selected product profile explicitly promotes them to required.
execution_policy.m1_minimum_security_kernel: Required before the first repository mutation: offline-by-default network, canonical path jail/protected roots, sanitized environment, structured and pinned executable resolution, a minimum local ExecutionIsolationBackend for repository-controlled code or fail-closed refusal, durable capability/action authorization journal, package/destructive/network denial unless explicitly granted, model/tool deadlines, minimal resource leases, process-tree cleanup, and unknown-outcome reconciliation.
execution_policy.roadmap_verification_command_note: verification_commands in this roadmap are human-readable implementation-agent instructions, not Plan IR runtime authorization. Sovereign runtime verification must resolve to digest-pinned tools and structured CommandSpec; no opaque shell string bypass is permitted.

resolution.dependencies: task.depends_on contains task IDs only; containing milestone.depends_on supplies milestone prerequisites.
resolution.schemas: Resolve from task.schemas when present, otherwise schema_contracts_by_task[task_id], otherwise an empty array only when the task introduces no durable/wire contract.
resolution.artifacts: Resolve from task.artifacts when present; otherwise use implementation changes under declared targets plus deterministic fixtures/tests and the task's completion_evidence outputs.
resolution.resource_constraints: Merge global_task_resource_constraints, containing milestone.resource_constraints when present, and resource_constraints_by_task[task_id]. A task may narrow but never silently widen output/RESOURCE_STRESS_TEST.md.
resolution.migration_steps: Use migration_steps_by_task[task_id], defaulting to an empty array only when the task introduces no durable compatibility transition. Derived indexes are rebuilt rather than promoted to canonical state.
resolution.completion: A task is complete only when dependencies are complete, listed tests and acceptance pass, verification commands have durable evidence, and every completion_evidence item exists with provenance.

machine_execution_contract.safety: No machine consumer may infer missing permission, rollback, resource, verification, migration, or completion semantics from model prose. Missing required effective data is a roadmap validation error.

stable_interface_contracts.invariant: Only deterministic Controller code owns authoritative execution transitions, authorization, budgets, verification, recovery truth, and completion.
ready/blocked are derived views and mutation dispatch is rechecked inside one current execution epoch.
Started attempts are immutable history; repair creates a new bounded attempt.
Dispatch requires current dependencies, evidence, baseline, checkpoint, permission possibility, and resource admission in one Controller epoch.
Compiler produces immutable candidate Plan IR revisions; PlanValidator and Controller activation remain deterministic authority.
No plan revision becomes active without deterministic Plan IR v1.2 structural, policy, evidence, and resource validation.
Filesystem/Git source is truth; retrieval indexes are fingerprinted, derived, and rebuildable.
Every model call receives a fresh bounded projection; persistent knowledge size never implies prompt size.
Provider details never enter Plan IR or Controller semantics; the M1 normal profile uses one physical local model at a time.
Tools expose declared structured effects and cannot self-authorize or lower deterministic risk.
Exact action authorization is durable, policy/epoch bound, and checked again before mutation.
Retained raw evidence means immutable post-ingress/redacted CAS bytes under explicit quotas.
Synopsis is bounded and derived, with expansion handles to retained evidence; expansion never reruns the tool.
Only fresh typed acceptance evidence can satisfy task or goal completion.
Checkpoints are monotonic hash/reference-verified snapshots over authoritative state and journal position.
Recovery replays authoritative events, reconciles unknown actions, and never blindly repeats uncertain side effects.
Heavy capability admission is lease based and preserves capability richness with runtime sparsity.
Memory is provenance/freshness governed evidence and never independent policy or repository truth.
Logical roles reuse the same physical model serially and cannot elevate permissions.
Skills are progressively loaded instructions/evidence and cannot grant authority.
Only SecretRef is durable/model-visible; resolved values are ephemeral action-only data and are redacted before persistence.
External intelligence is optional untrusted advisory evidence with explicit export policy and zero tool, approval, or completion authority.

global_task_resource_constraints: Target the MacBook Air M1/8GB profile in output/RESOURCE_STRESS_TEST.md unless a task explicitly names a stricter optional-adapter calibration profile.
Normal operation uses at most one local LLM process and one mutation at a time; heavyweight capabilities require Controller leases and forbidden/unknown heavy pairs serialize.
No task may make cloud, internet, browser, semantic embeddings, CodeGraph/wiki, or a second resident local model a hidden prerequisite for core correctness.
Context is bounded: normal 8k input, 12k bounded planning/review only after calibration, and 16k un-overridden M1 ceiling with no automatic growth beyond it.
When live pressure, swap-out/compressor growth, thermal state, or measured process footprint is worse than the nominal arithmetic budget, the stricter live admission result wins.

M1-T03: One local 3B-4B model process maximum; record target-machine steady/peak/context growth and unload residual before M1 closes.
M1-T04: Repository-controlled code runs only when the configured local isolation backend enforces the declared boundary; otherwise the action fails closed.
M1-T05: Retained evidence and model-facing synopses are separately quota bounded; compression must not require an unbounded in-memory log.
M1-T06: Normal packet target is 8k input and the M1 ceiling is 16k; context insufficiency triggers better retrieval, compression, split, or replan rather than automatic growth.
M1-T10: Exactly one MODEL lease; no embedder/browser/knowledge adapter; compiler calls are charged to plan/controller model-call and wall-time budgets.
M1-T07: One mutation at a time and Controller outer budgets dominate provider/tool retry loops.
M1-T08: Recovery launches no new mutation until checkpoint, journal, process ownership, and unknown-action truth are reconciled.
M1-T09: Repair remains inside the same task budget and conjunctive max_attempts/same_failure_limit.
M2-T01: Index builds are bounded heavy jobs with measured batch/cache/WAL footprint; no resident embedder.
M2-T02: Parser/index batches never retain a whole large-repository AST; no resident embedder.
M2-T03: No semantic/embedder lease; retrieval stops after sufficient cheaper evidence.
M3-T02: Planning calls obey model-call, wall-time, context, task-count, plan-revision, and per-scope replan ceilings.
M4-T02: Memory retrieval remains filter/signature/lexical first and prompt-token bounded; no resident embedder.
M6-T01: Live pressure/swap-out/compressor/thermal state overrides arithmetic admission and unknown heavy pairs serialize.
M7-T01: Embedder is demand-loaded and normally serialized with MODEL, browser, and heavy build; <=50k hot vectors default and <=100k active corpus ceiling absent calibrated override.
M7-T03: Deterministic browser is demand-loaded, initially one-tab, normally serialized with MODEL/build/embedder, and zero-resident after lease release.
M7-T04: Adaptive browser is admitted only after measured combined calibration; its inner loop cannot exceed Controller budgets.
M8-T02: Use the provisional optional-knowledge admission ceiling until Apple-arm64 calibration replaces it; serialize with other heavy residents while uncalibrated.
M9-T04: Soak/checkpoint tests must preserve host headroom and may defer work under pressure; they must not intentionally require sustained swap thrash.

M0-T02: Initialize a fresh database through numbered transactional migrations and record the schema version.
Before a destructive/failed migration test, create an exact fixture backup and prove rollback leaves the previous version readable.
M1-T01: Active writes emit Plan IR v1.2 only; retain explicit version dispatch so M9-T03 can read/migrate v1.1 fixtures without widening authority.
M2-T01: Treat lexical index state as derived; incompatible index schema/version invalidates and rebuilds from current source rather than migrating canonical truth.
M2-T02: Treat symbol/dependency graph state as derived; incompatible parser/schema versions trigger bounded source-fingerprint rebuild.
M4-T01: Add memory tables through a numbered transactional SQLite migration with backup and rollback fixture.
Do not synthesize trust or provenance for ambiguous legacy data.
M4-T03: Install projection-outbox schema before asynchronous projection writes; after upgrade, replay/rebuild projections from canonical memory.
M6-T03: Migrate secret handles/provider metadata only; never copy resolved secret values into Sovereign durable state.
M7-T01: Vector projection is disposable: model/dimension/version changes invalidate and rebuild vectors from canonical source/memory.
M7-T02: Adapter install/remove leaves core durable state unchanged; adapter-owned caches are disposable.
M7-T03: Default ephemeral browser profiles need no migration; explicitly granted persistent profile metadata is separately versioned.
M7-T04: Adaptive adapter install/remove leaves core schema unchanged; adapter caches are disposable.
M8-T02: CodeGraph state is derived and may be dropped/rebuilt across adapter version changes.
M8-T03: Wiki/document assets are derived and rebuild from source hashes across incompatible versions.
M9-T03: Back up durable SQLite/CAS metadata before upgrade.
Read and migrate Plan IR v1.1 under v1.2 without synthesizing broader authority absent from the source plan.
Apply numbered durable-state migrations transactionally and prove rollback/old-reader diagnostics on failure.
Rebuild disposable FTS/symbol/dependency/vector/wiki/CodeGraph projections from canonical state.
Run ModelBackend conformance before switching providers and roll provider configuration back independently of Plan IR/state.

milestone_gates: A simple natural-language fixture goal is compiled by M1-T10 from bounded exact repository evidence into validated Plan IR v1.2, then executed through the real Controller/tool/evidence/verifier loop, checkpointed, killed, and resumed successfully. migration_and_evolution_rules: All durable schemas carry explicit versions and forward migrations; every durable migration has a backup/rollback or explicit non-reversible fail-closed procedure before activation.
Plan IR active writes use v1.2. The compatibility reader/migration path accepts v1.1 fixtures without inventing authority absent from the original plan.
Plan revisions and retained post-ingress/redacted raw evidence are immutable historical artifacts; secret-bearing pre-redaction bytes are not persisted for fidelity.
FTS/symbol/dependency/vector/wiki/CodeGraph indexes are derived and rebuildable; migrate canonical metadata when needed and rebuild derived projections rather than treating them as truth.
Vector model/dimension/version changes invalidate the corresponding projection and rebuild it under a new version; old vector bytes are never reinterpreted as a new embedding space.
Memory migrations preserve provenance, scope, trust, freshness, supersession/conflict links, and outbox consistency; ambiguous legacy meaning is not silently promoted.
Provider-specific fields stay inside adapter-owned configuration, never Plan IR semantics; provider swaps must pass ModelBackend conformance before activation.
Optional adapter install/remove cannot make core state unreadable or core tests depend on the adapter; adapter caches/projections are disposable unless explicitly governed otherwise.
Experimental adapters launch out-of-process until their stability/security/resource behavior is established.
A new feature may not become always-resident on M1 merely because it exists; ResourceGovernor needs an explicit lease type and measured profile.
A new skill or role may narrow behavior but never grant permission.
A migration that changes task or memory meaning must preserve provenance and old-reader diagnostics.
Optional adapter milestones/tasks remain nonblocking until an explicit product profile promotes them to required; promotion must be recorded rather than inferred from dependency presence.
roadmap_completion_gate: The Controller, rather than the model, owns every authoritative execution transition.

The first complete M1 vertical slice starts from a simple natural-language goal and canonical PlanCompiler output; hand-authored Plan IR alone cannot satisfy the vertical-slice proof, while FTS/semantic/browser/memory/roles remain later capabilities.
All core task execution works offline after required local model/tool acquisition with a replaceable local ModelBackend.
M1 closure includes a mandatory real local 3B-4B-class model smoke on the target 8GB machine; fake backends remain deterministic CI/unit-test tools only.
A weak local model completes the reference tasks using bounded evidence packets rather than repository/chat dumps.

Plan IR v1.2 dependency bindings, evidence-satisfaction/freshness rules, acceptance freshness, deterministic retry exhaustion, typed rollback verification, untrusted-code isolation, audit/external-intelligence policies, and per-call deadline fields are enforced by PlanValidator/Controller tests.

Plan validation, execution-vs-plan failure, bounded smallest-scope replanning, stale-plan revalidation, journal-based restart recovery, verification, checkpoint/corruption handling, and completion governance are proven by tests.
Memory is provenance-aware and never a silent policy authority.

Retained raw tool evidence means recoverable post-ingress/redacted bytes under explicit spool/storage quotas and truncation evidence; model-facing synopses are versioned and expandable by digest/range without rerunning the tool.
Repository/source fingerprints invalidate stale index and memory projections before they can be injected as current facts.

Retrieval routing is deterministic and gap-driven: exact/path, lexical, symbol, dependency, diff, and episodic routes stop when sufficient; optional semantic retrieval is bounded candidate generation only after a recorded cheaper-route gap or inherently fuzzy query.
Context telemetry records candidate/deduped/serialized tokens and verified-usefulness metrics by route so generic vector RAG cannot hide behind aggregate recall metrics.

The M1/8 GB resource governor prevents conflicting heavyweight residents and uses live host pressure plus swap/compressor deltas, calibrated lease footprints, and hysteresis as the final admission guard rather than additive RSS or absolute swap-used alone.

Security fixtures prove repository/web/tool/external-model content cannot self-grant permissions; repository-controlled code cannot bypass declared filesystem/network/secret boundaries; Git/package/browser hidden execution is governed; and audit/checkpoint corruption, rollback ambiguity, unknown side effects, or runaway budgets fail closed.

External intelligence is disabled by default, sends no resolved secrets or unrestricted repository/raw-log content by default, has no tool/approval/completion authority, and can be absent without changing core correctness.
Optional semantic/browser/knowledge/external-model adapters can be absent without breaking or blocking core tests/release.

freeze.amendment_scope: Sequencing-only architecture/roadmap/scenario alignment. Moves the canonical minimal PlanCompiler into the first complete M1 vertical slice, makes Controller execution consume compiler-produced Plan IR, declares stable destination interface ownership up front, and adds machine-resolved schema/artifact/resource/migration/completion semantics. M3 now deepens the same compiler rather than introducing it. The security/autonomy/runtime semantics established in 2026-09-12.6 are unchanged; Plan IR remains v1.2; RESOURCE_STRESS_TEST remains 2026-09-12.3; optional-track/local-first/one-model/security boundaries are unchanged.
